metadata.title: On Response-Adaptive Targeting Strategies for Multi-Treatment Experiments

nodes.name: Index set [K]
nodes.statement: In the following we denote \([K]:= \left\{1, \dots, K\right\}\).

nodes.name: Assignment vector
nodes.statement: For each patient $m$, let \(X_m = (X_{m,1}, \ldots, X_{m,K})\) denote the assignment vector, where $X_{m,k}=1$ indicates that the patient \(m\) is assigned to arm \(k \in [K]\) and $X_{m,k}=0$ otherwise, thus we have $\sum_{k=1}^{K} X_{m,k} = 1$.

nodes.name: Treatment responses
nodes.statement: Consider the sequence of \textit{i.i.d.} random variables \(\left\{\xi_{m,k}, m=1, \dots\right\}\) where \(\xi_{m,k}\) is the response of the \(m^{th}\) patient on treatment \(k\).

nodes.name: Treatment mean parameter
nodes.statement: For a treatment $k \in [K]$, the parameter of interest in this paper is the expectation of these responses, we denote it as \(\theta_k := \mathbb{E}\left[\xi_{1,k}\right]\).

nodes.name: Parameter vector
nodes.statement: We also define the vector of these parameters, \(\Theta = (\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_K) \in \mathbb{R}^K\).

nodes.name: Treatment counts
nodes.statement: The total number of patients assigned to each treatment up to time $n$ is denoted by \(N_n = (N_{n,1}, \ldots, N_{n,K})\) where \(N_{n,k} = \sum_{j=1}^n X_{j,k}\).

nodes.name: Observed allocation proportions
nodes.statement: The normalized vector $N_n/n$ represents the observed allocation proportions at time $n$.

nodes.name: Extension to multi-dimensional parameters
nodes.statement: Prior work often consider a more general setting in which both the observation $\xi_{m,k}$ and the parameter of the distribution $\theta_k$ can be multi-dimensional (e.g., $\theta_k$ is the mean and covariance of a Gaussian arm). For the sake of clarity, we focus our investigation on the (doubly) uni-dimensional case, for distribution parameterized by their means. This encompasses the example of arms that belong to a one-dimensional exponential family, that has received particular attention in the multi-armed bandit literature \citep{KLUCBJournal,garivier2016optimal}. However, our analysis and results extend to these more complex settings without substantial modification.

nodes.name: Filtration of assignments and outcomes
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}_m = \sigma\!\left((X_i,\xi_i)_{1 \le i \le m}\right)$ denote the filtration generated by the treatment assignments and observed outcomes of the first $m$ patients.

nodes.name: Response-Adaptive Randomization (RAR) procedure
nodes.statement: A \textit{RAR} procedure is a sequence $(p_m)_{m\ge1}$ of $\mathcal{F}_m$-measurable random vectors taking values in the probability simplex \[ \Delta_K := \left\{ p \in [0,1]^K : \sum_{k=1}^K p_k = 1 \right\}. \] At step $m+1$, the treatment assignment $X_{m+1}$ is drawn conditionally on $\mathcal{F}_m$ according to $p_m$, that is, \[ \mathbb{P}(X_{m+1} = k \mid \mathcal{F}_m) = p_{m,k}, \qquad k = 1,\dots,K. \]
nodes.statement_short: A RAR procedure is a sequence of adapted allocation probability vectors in the simplex from which each next assignment is drawn.

nodes.name: Target function and target allocation
nodes.statement: Given some target function $\rho : \mathcal{H} \rightarrow \Delta_K$, i.e. a function such that, for any $z \in \mathcal{H}$, \[ \rho(z) = (\rho_1(z), \ldots, \rho_K(z)) \] satisfies $\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho_{k}(z)=1$, we propose in this work RAR procedures under which the empirical allocation $N_n/n$ converges to the target allocation $v := \rho(\Theta)$.
nodes.statement_short: A target function maps parameters to the simplex; the goal is $N_n/n \to v=\rho(\Theta)$.

nodes.name: Adaptive targeting mechanism
nodes.statement: We refer to these procedures as adaptive targeting mechanisms.

nodes.name: Little-o in probability
nodes.statement: More formally, for a sequence $\{X_n\}$ of random variables and $\left(a_n\right)_{n \geq 1}$ a sequence of positive real numbers. We say that $X_n = o_p(a_n)$ if for all $\varepsilon > 0$, \(\lim_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}\!\left( \frac{|X_n|}{a_n} > \varepsilon \right) = 0.\)

nodes.name: Big-O in probability
nodes.statement: We say that $X_n = O_p(a_n)$ if for all $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $M > 0$ such that \(\limsup_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}\!\left( \frac{|X_n|}{a_n} > M \right) \leq \varepsilon.\)

nodes.name: Regularized sequential estimator
nodes.statement: Given some initial value $\theta_{0,k}$, the sequential estimator for treatment $k$ at stage $m$ is \begin{equation} \hat{\theta}_{m,k} := \frac{\sum_{j=1}^m X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} + \theta_{0,k}}{N_{m,k}+1}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Sequential estimator formula
nodes.statement: \hat{\theta}_{m,k} := \frac{\sum_{j=1}^m X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} + \theta_{0,k}}{N_{m,k}+1}.
nodes.label: eq:dbcd-estimator

nodes.name: Plug-in target estimator
nodes.statement: Letting \(\hat{\Theta}_m := (\hat{\theta}_{m,1}, \ldots, \hat{\theta}_{m,K}),\) our estimate of the target allocation $v=\rho(\Theta)$ is the plug-in estimator $\hat{\rho}_m := \rho(\hat{\Theta}_m).$

nodes.name: Bahadur-type representation of alternative estimators
nodes.statement: For our analysis to go through, an alternative estimator of $\theta_k$ can be used, as long as it has the Bahadur-type representation, i.e., it can be written \begin{equation} \hat{\theta}_{m,k} = \frac{1}{N_{m,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{m}X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} + o(N_{m,k}^{-1/2}),\quad \text{as } m\to\infty. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Bahadur-type representation
nodes.statement: \hat{\theta}_{m,k} = \frac{1}{N_{m,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{m}X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} + o(N_{m,k}^{-1/2}),\quad \text{as } m\to\infty.
nodes.label: eq:bahadur-estimator

nodes.name: ERADE
nodes.statement: The ERADE design, introduced by \cite{hu2009efficient} for $K=2$ uses a parameter $\alpha \in [0,1)$ and works as follows. It compares the current empirical allocation to arm $1$, $N_{m,1}/m$ to its estimated target $\hat{\rho}_{m,1}$ and whenever $\frac{N_{m,1}}{m}>\hat\rho_{m,1}$ it reduces the probability to select arm $1$ in the next round by setting $p_{m+1,1}=\alpha \hat\rho_{m,1}$. More precisely, it sets \begin{equation*} p_{m+1,1} = \begin{cases} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,1}, & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m > \hat{\rho}_m, \\[6pt] \hat{\rho}_{m,1}, & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m = \hat{\rho}_m, \\[6pt] 1 - \alpha(1 - \hat{\rho}_{m,1}), & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m < \hat{\rho}_m, \end{cases} \end{equation*} and $p_{m+1,2}=1-p_{m+1,1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Two-arm ERADE: if arm 1 is over-sampled relative to its estimated target, sample it with probability $\alpha\hat\rho$, else boost it.

nodes.name: Compare arm 1's empirical proportion with its estimated targ
nodes.statement: It compares the current empirical allocation to arm $1$, $N_{m,1}/m$ to its estimated target $\hat{\rho}_{m,1}$
nodes.statement_short: Compare arm 1's empirical proportion with its estimated target

nodes.name: Set arm 1's probability by the three-case ERADE rule
nodes.statement: More precisely, it sets \begin{equation*} p_{m+1,1} = \begin{cases} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,1}, & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m > \hat{\rho}_m, \\[6pt] \hat{\rho}_{m,1}, & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m = \hat{\rho}_m, \\[6pt] 1 - \alpha(1 - \hat{\rho}_{m,1}), & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m < \hat{\rho}_m, \end{cases} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Set arm 1's probability by the three-case ERADE rule

nodes.name: ERADE allocation rule
nodes.statement: p_{m+1,1} = \begin{cases} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,1}, & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m > \hat{\rho}_m, \\[6pt] \hat{\rho}_{m,1}, & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m = \hat{\rho}_m, \\[6pt] 1 - \alpha(1 - \hat{\rho}_{m,1}), & \text{if } N_{m,1}/m < \hat{\rho}_m, \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:erade

nodes.name: Assign the remaining probability to arm 2
nodes.statement_short: Assign the remaining probability to arm 2

nodes.name: alpha-Rebalancing Targeting Strategy (alphaRTS)
nodes.statement: Let $K\geq 2$ and $\alpha\in[0,1)$. A design is an $\alpha$-Rebalancing Targeting Strategy ($\alpha$RTS) if it a RAR procedure whose allocation probabilities $p_{m+1}=(p_{m+1,1},\dots,p_{m+1,K}) \in \Delta_K$ satisfy the following: for all $m \geq Km_0$, \begin{align} &\forall k \in [K], \ \left(\frac{N_{m,k}}{m}>\hat\rho_{m,k}\quad \Longrightarrow\quad p_{m+1,k}\le \alpha\,\hat\rho_{m,k}\right) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: A RAR design is $\alpha$RTS if any over-sampled arm gets allocation probability at most $\alpha$ times its estimated target.

nodes.name: Throttling condition
nodes.statement: &\forall k \in [K], \ \left(\frac{N_{m,k}}{m}>\hat\rho_{m,k}\quad \Longrightarrow\quad p_{m+1,k}\le \alpha\,\hat\rho_{m,k}\right)
nodes.label: eq:throttle

nodes.name: Burn-in parameter m_0
nodes.statement: The parameter $m_0$ (sometimes called burn-in in a clinical trial context) is the number of initial samples from each arm that may be taken before starting adaptive randomization. It is included for practical purposes only and doesn't influence the proofs. We can safely take $m_0 = 0$ if $\theta_0$, the regularization parameter of the estimator, is chosen in an appropriate way.

nodes.name: Distance Based Allocation
nodes.statement: Given $\alpha \in [0,1)$, for all $m\geq Km_0$, for all $k \in [K]$, \begin{equation*} p_{m+1,k} \;=\; \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \;+\; (1-\alpha)\, \frac{\delta_{m,k}}{\sum_{i=1}^K \delta_{m,i}}, \ \text{ where } \ \delta_{m,k} \;=\; \max\!\left(0,\ \hat{\rho}_{m,k} - \frac{N_{m,k}}{m}\right)\;. \end{equation*} If for all $j$, $\delta_{m,j}=0$, then for every $j \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$, we choose \(p_{m+1,j} \;=\; \hat{\rho}_{m,j}.\) We use a distance-based design to ensure that arms that deviates the most from their target allocation are corrected more aggressively.
nodes.statement_short: Boost under-sampled arms in proportion to their deficit $\delta_{m,k}$ to the estimated target.

nodes.name: Distance-based allocation rule
nodes.statement: p_{m+1,k} \;=\; \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \;+\; (1-\alpha)\, \frac{\delta_{m,k}}{\sum_{i=1}^K \delta_{m,i}}, \ \text{ where } \ \delta_{m,k} \;=\; \max\!\left(0,\ \hat{\rho}_{m,k} - \frac{N_{m,k}}{m}\right)\;.
nodes.label: eq:example

nodes.name: ERADE 2025
nodes.statement: Given $\alpha \in [0,1)$\footnote{The paper actually set $\alpha \in (0,1)$ but there is no need for that}, for all $m\geq Km_0$, $k \in [K]$, \[ p_{m+1,k} = \begin{cases} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k} & \text{ if } \ \dfrac{N_{m,k}}{m} > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}, \\[6pt] \hat{\rho}_{m,k} & \text{ if } \ \dfrac{N_{m,k}}{m} = \hat{\rho}_{m,k}, \\[6pt] \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + (1-\alpha)\displaystyle\frac{\sum_{j \in S}\hat{\rho}_{m,j}}{|T|} & \text{ if } \ \dfrac{N_{m,k}}{m} < \hat{\rho}_{m,k}. \end{cases} \] where $S = \left\{ j \; \middle| \; \dfrac{N_{m,j}}{m} > \rho_{m,j} \right\}$ is the set of over-sampled arms, $T = \left\{ j \; \middle| \; \dfrac{N_{m,j}}{m} < \rho_{m,j} \right\}$ is the set of under-sampled arms and $|T|$ denotes the cardinal of set $T$.
nodes.statement_short: Multi-arm ERADE: throttle over-sampled arms and spread the freed mass equally over under-sampled arms.

nodes.name: Interpolated D-Tracking
nodes.statement: Inspired by the D-Tracking rule of \cite{garivier2016optimal}, we define for a parameter $\alpha \geq 0$ the \textit{Interpolated D-tracking} rule by \begin{equation} p_{m+1,k} = \alpha \hat \rho_{m,k} + (1-\alpha)\mathbf 1_{\{k=k^\star\}}, \end{equation} where \(k^\star = \arg\max_{a\in[K]} \left\{ m\hat \rho_{m,a}-N_{m,a} \right\} \). The quantity $m\hat \rho_{m,a}-N_{m,a}$ measures the deficit of arm $a$ relative to its target allocation. Hence, $k^\star$ is the arm whose current number of draws is furthest below its prescribed proportion. For all $\alpha$, we can easily verify that this design belongs to the $\alpha$RTS family. It clearly satisfies $\sum_{k=1}^{K} p_{m+1,k}=1$. Then, for any arm $k$ that is over-sampled, i.e. for which $N_{m,k}/m > \hat \rho_{m,k}$, we have $m\hat \rho_{m,k}-N_{m,k} < 0$, which implies that $k\neq k^\star$ and \(p_{m+1,k} = \alpha \hat \rho_{m,k}\). In the special case where $\alpha=0$, \eqref{eq:alpha-d-tracking} reduces to \(p_{m+1,k} = \mathbf 1_{\{k=k^\star\}},\) which coincides with the original D-tracking rule of \citet{garivier2016optimal} without including its forced exploration component (which will be discussed again in Section~\ref{sec:alpha-rts-fe}).
nodes.statement_short: Mix $\alpha\hat\rho$ with a point mass on the arm of largest deficit; $\alpha=0$ is D-Tracking without forced exploration.

nodes.name: Interpolated D-Tracking rule
nodes.statement: p_{m+1,k} = \alpha \hat \rho_{m,k} + (1-\alpha)\mathbf 1_{\{k=k^\star\}},
nodes.label: eq:alpha-d-tracking

nodes.name: Interpolated D-Tracking is an alphaRTS
nodes.statement: For all $\alpha$, we can easily verify that this design belongs to the $\alpha$RTS family.
conclusions: this design belongs to the $\alpha$RTS family

nodes.name: Proof that Interpolated D-Tracking is an alphaRTS
nodes.statement: It clearly satisfies $\sum_{k=1}^{K} p_{m+1,k}=1$. Then, for any arm $k$ that is over-sampled, i.e. for which $N_{m,k}/m > \hat \rho_{m,k}$, we have $m\hat \rho_{m,k}-N_{m,k} < 0$, which implies that $k\neq k^\star$ and \(p_{m+1,k} = \alpha \hat \rho_{m,k}\).
nodes.statement_short: Direct check: probabilities sum to one and an over-sampled arm is never $k^\star$, so it gets $\alpha\hat\rho_{m,k}$.

nodes.name: Condition A (finite second moments)
nodes.statement: For treatment \(k \in [K]\) the corresponding response \(\xi_{1,k}\) satisfies $ E|\xi_{1,k}|^{2} < \infty $.

nodes.name: Condition B (smooth non-sparse target)
nodes.statement: The target function $\rho$ and the regularization parameter $\theta_0$ of the estimator satisfy the following. Let $I_k = \{\theta_k\} \bigcup V_k$ where $V_k$ is the set of all possible values that can be observed for the estimator $\hat\theta_{n,k}$, for all $n$ and all realizations of the responses $\{\xi_{j,k}\}$. The domain $\mathcal{H} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^K$ of the target function is open and contains $I_1\times \dots \times I_K$. Moreover: \begin{itemize} \item \(\rho\) is twice differentiable on $\mathcal{H}$, \item for all $z \in I_1\times \dots \times I_k$, \ \(\rho(z) \in (0,1)^K\). \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The target is twice differentiable on an open domain containing all possible estimates, and takes values in $(0,1)^K$ there.

nodes.name: Strong consistency and rates
nodes.statement: Under conditions \hyperlink{CA}{\textbf{A}}--\hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}}, for \(n \to \infty\), \[ \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\xrightarrow{\text{a.s.}}v_k,\qquad \hat\Theta_n-\Theta = O\!\Big(\sqrt{\frac{\log\log n}{n}}\Big)\text{ a.s.},\qquad n(\hat\rho_n-v)=O\!\big(\sqrt{n\log\log n}\big)\text{ a.s.} \]
nodes.statement_short: Under A-B, allocation proportions converge a.s. to the target and estimators converge at the LIL rate.
conclusions: \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\xrightarrow{\text{a.s.}}v_k,\qquad \hat\Theta_n-\Theta = O\!\Big(\sqrt{\frac{\log\log n}{n}}\Big)\text{ a.s.},\qquad n(\hat\rho_n-v)=O\!\big(\sqrt{n\log\log n}\big)\text{ a.s.} \]
nodes.label: thm:LLN

nodes.name: Asymptotic normality of alphaRTS
nodes.statement: We introduce the following notation \begin{itemize} \item \(G := \nabla (\rho)\big|_{\Theta}\) denotes the gradient of the target allocation $\rho$ with respect to $\Theta$ \item \(V_k := \mathbb{V}ar[\xi_{1,k}]\) is the variance for treatment \(k\) response \item \(V := diag\left(\frac{1}{v_1}V_1, \dots, \frac{1}{v_K}V_K\right)\) is a diagonal matrix collecting the scaled variances \item \(\Omega := \begin{pmatrix} GVG^{\top } & GVG^{\top } \\ GVG^{\top } & GVG^{\top } \end{pmatrix}\) is a block matrix built from \(GVG^{\top }\) \end{itemize} Under conditions \hyperlink{CA}{\textbf{A}}--\hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}}, we have as \(n \to \infty\) \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For every \(k \in [K]\), \begin{align} |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= o_P(\sqrt{n}) \\ |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= O(\sqrt{n \log\log n})\quad a.s. \\ N_{n,k}-n v_k&=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\quad a.s. \end{align} \item The asymptotic normality results: \begin{align} \sqrt{n}(\hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta) &\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} N(0,V),\\ \begin{pmatrix} \sqrt{n} \left( \frac{N_n}{n} - v \right)\\ \sqrt{n} (\hat{\rho}_n - v) \end{pmatrix} &\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} \mathcal{N}(0,\Omega). \end{align} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Under A-B, $N_n-n\hat\rho_n$ is $o_P(\sqrt n)$ and the estimators and allocation proportions are jointly asymptotically normal.
conclusions: For every \(k \in [K]\), \begin{align} |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= o_P(\sqrt{n}) \\ |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= O(\sqrt{n \log\log n})\quad a.s. \\ N_{n,k}-n v_k&=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\quad a.s. \end{align}

The asymptotic normality results: \begin{align} \sqrt{n}(\hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta) &\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} N(0,V),\\ \begin{pmatrix} \sqrt{n} \left( \frac{N_n}{n} - v \right)\\ \sqrt{n} (\hat{\rho}_n - v) \end{pmatrix} &\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} \mathcal{N}(0,\Omega). \end{align}
nodes.label: thm:normality-gen-erade

nodes.name: Tracking error o_P(sqrt n)
nodes.statement: |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= o_P(\sqrt{n})
nodes.label: eq:thm-res-1

nodes.name: Tracking error LIL rate
nodes.statement: |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= O(\sqrt{n \log\log n})\quad a.s.
nodes.label: eq:thm-res-2

nodes.name: Allocation LIL rate
nodes.statement: N_{n,k}-n v_k&=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\quad a.s.
nodes.label: eq:thm-res-3

nodes.name: CLT for estimators
nodes.statement: \sqrt{n}(\hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta) &\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} N(0,V),
nodes.label: eq:thm-res-4

nodes.name: Joint CLT for proportions and plug-in target
nodes.statement: \begin{pmatrix} \sqrt{n} \left( \frac{N_n}{n} - v \right)\\ \sqrt{n} (\hat{\rho}_n - v) \end{pmatrix} &\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} \mathcal{N}(0,\Omega).
nodes.label: eq:thm-res-5

nodes.name: Asymptotic efficiency of alphaRTS
nodes.statement: A direct consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm:normality-gen-erade} is that the empirical allocation proportion $N_n/n$ is an asymptotically efficient estimator of the target $v$, at least when the arms distribution belong to an exponential family. Indeed, under this assumption, Theorem 1 of \cite{hu2006asymptotically} provides a lower bound on the asymptotic variance of $N_n/n$ as an estimator of $v$ under any RAR procedure, that is \[G\,I(\Theta)^{-1}\,G^{\top }\] where \(I(\Theta) = \mathrm{diag}\left(v_1 I_1(\theta_1), \dots, v_K I_K(\theta_K)\right)\) and \(I_k(\theta_k)\) is the Fisher information for a single observation from treatment \(k \in [K]\). The condition $\mathbb{V}ar(\xi_{1,k}) = I_k(\theta_k)^{-1}$ is naturally satisfied for regular one-parameter exponential families when the parameter of interest $\theta_k$ is the mean parameter (see Proposition~\ref{prop:exp-fam} in Appendix~\ref{appnC}). Hence the minimal asymptotic variance is equal to $GVG^{\top}$, which is the asymptotic variance under any $\alpha$RTS design when conditions \hyperlink{CA}{\textbf{A}}--\hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}} are satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Combining Theorem 4.2 with the Hu-Zhang-He lower bound, $N_n/n$ attains the minimal asymptotic variance $GVG^\top$ for exponential families.
assumptions: at least when the arms distribution belong to an exponential family
conclusions: the empirical allocation proportion $N_n/n$ is an asymptotically efficient estimator of the target $v$

nodes.name: Hu-Zhang-He asymptotic variance lower bound
nodes.statement: Indeed, under this assumption, Theorem 1 of \cite{hu2006asymptotically} provides a lower bound on the asymptotic variance of $N_n/n$ as an estimator of $v$ under any RAR procedure, that is \[G\,I(\Theta)^{-1}\,G^{\top }\] where \(I(\Theta) = \mathrm{diag}\left(v_1 I_1(\theta_1), \dots, v_K I_K(\theta_K)\right)\) and \(I_k(\theta_k)\) is the Fisher information for a single observation from treatment \(k \in [K]\).
conclusions: provides a lower bound on the asymptotic variance of $N_n/n$ as an estimator of $v$ under any RAR procedure, that is \[G\,I(\Theta)^{-1}\,G^{\top }\]

nodes.name: Conditional probabilities, assignment martingale and auxiliary process U
nodes.statement: We first introduce the natural extension to $k$ arms of the quantities introduced in the analysis of ERADE: \begin{itemize} \item $p_{m,k} := \mathbb{E}[X_{m,k} \mid \mathcal{F}_{m-1}]$, the conditional probability of assigning treatment $k$ at step $m$ \item $M_{n,k} := \sum_{m=1}^{n}(X_{m,k} - p_{m,k})$, a martingale capturing the deviation of the actual assignment from its conditional expectation \end{itemize} as well as \[U_{n,k} = \sum_{m=1}^{n-1} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + M_{n,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k}\;.\]

nodes.name: Generic sufficient conditions for alphaRTS asymptotics
nodes.statement: Consider a RAR procedure under which there exists a sequence of random variables $(\ell_{n,k})_{n,k}$ satisfying the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item for all $k\in [K]$, \(\left(\ell_{n,k}\right)_{n \geq 1}\) is a non-decreasing sequence and for all \(n \in \mathbb{N}: \,\ell_{n,k} \leq n\) \item for all $k\in [K]$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, \begin{equation} N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq 1+N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} \end{equation} \item for all $k\in [K]$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, \begin{equation} N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} = o(\sqrt{n}) \ a.s. \quad \end{equation} \end{enumerate} Then the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} and Theorem~\ref{thm:normality-gen-erade} hold.
nodes.statement_short: Any RAR procedure with a non-decreasing hitting-time sequence $\ell_{n,k}$ satisfying (ii)-(iii) enjoys the conclusions of Theorems 4.1-4.2.
assumptions: Consider a RAR procedure under which there exists a sequence of random variables $(\ell_{n,k})_{n,k}$ satisfying the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item for all $k\in [K]$, \(\left(\ell_{n,k}\right)_{n \geq 1}\) is a non-decreasing sequence and for all \(n \in \mathbb{N}: \,\ell_{n,k} \leq n\) \item for all $k\in [K]$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, \begin{equation} N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq 1+N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} \end{equation} \item for all $k\in [K]$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, \begin{equation} N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} = o(\sqrt{n}) \ a.s. \quad \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: Then the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} and Theorem~\ref{thm:normality-gen-erade} hold.
nodes.label: lem:generic-conditions-main

nodes.name: Hitting-time inequality (sketch)

nodes.name: Proof sketch of the generic conditions lemma
nodes.statement: We now briefly sketch the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:generic-conditions-main}. The detailed proof that Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} holds can be found in Appendix~\ref{proof:thm1}. The first step to establish the convergence of the empirical proportions is to show that the sequence $\hat{\rho}_n$ has a limit $u \in \Delta_K$ that is non-sparse, i.e. that satisfies $u_k \neq 0$ for all $k$. The argument there relies on both Condition \hyperlink{CA}{\textbf{A}} (to apply the law of large number) and Condition \hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}}. Then, combining Inequalities~\eqref{eq:prelim-sketch} and \eqref{eq:condition-sketch} yields that for all $k$ \begin{equation} \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq \frac{U_{n,k}- U_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n} + o\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right).\end{equation} Starting from the definition of $U_{n,k}$, we can now apply the law of large number to the martingale $M_n$ and use the convergence of $\hat{\rho}_{n}$ to prove that $\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty} \frac{U_{n,k}}{n} = -(1-\alpha)u_k \in (0,1)$. Some algebra (Lemma~\ref{lem:convergence}) further permits to show that the right-hand side of Equation~\eqref{step-main} tends to zero. Using that both $N_n/n$ and $\hat{\rho}_n$ are probability vectors, it follows that $\lim_{n\rightarrow 0} \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k} = 0$ and that ${N_{n}}/{n}$ also converges to $u \in (0,1)^K$. A straightforward consequence is that $\forall k \in [K], N_{n,k} \to \infty$ a.s., hence $\hat{\Theta}_n$ converges to $\Theta$ and by continuity of \(\rho\) we obtain that \(\hat{\rho}_n = \rho(\hat{\Theta}_n) \to \rho(\Theta) = v \in (0,1)^K\), hence for all $k$, \[ \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} = \lim_{n \to \infty} \hat{\rho}_{n,k} = v_k\;. \] The convergence rates follows from the Law of Iterated Logarithm. \smallskip The detailed proof that Theorem~\ref{thm:normality-gen-erade} holds can be found in Appendix~\ref{proof:thm2}. To get the more precise rates in statement (i), we need a more careful control on the increment of the auxiliary process $U_{n,k}$. Namely, we prove through a series of (rather technical) lemmas that \[ U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_{n,k},k}\leq o_p(\sqrt n), \qquad U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_{n,k},k}\leq O(\sqrt{n\log\log n}) \quad a.s. \] which yields the following using the identities $\sum_{k=1}^K N_{n,k}=n$ and $\sum_{k=1}^K \hat\rho_{n,k}=1$: \[ N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k}=o_p(\sqrt n)\;. \] This proves the statements \eqref{eq:thm-res-1}--\eqref{eq:thm-res-2}. Combined with the rate \(n(\hat\rho_n-v)=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\) from Theorem \ref{thm:LLN} yields \eqref{eq:thm-res-3}. To establish the asymptotic normality in (ii), we prove the following lemma that gives the joint CLT of the components of the estimator \(\hat{\Theta}_n\) scaled with \(\sqrt{N_{n,k}}\). The proof of Lemma \ref{lem:componentwise} relies on a martingale-CLT argument and is given in Appendix~\ref{proof:thm2}. \begin{restatable}{lemma}{jointcltlemma}[Joint CLT with Componentwise Scaling] Consider a RAR procedure under which $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ a.s. for all $k \in [K]$, then we have \[ D_n(\hat\Theta_n-\Theta)\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} \mathcal N\!\big(0,\mathrm{diag}\left(V_1,\dots,V_K\right)\big) \] where $D_n:=\mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{N_{n,1}},\dots,\sqrt{N_{n,K}})\;.$ \end{restatable} Using the fact that \(\sqrt n D_n^{-1}\) converges to \(\mathrm{diag}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{v_1}},\ldots,\frac{1}{\sqrt{v_K}}\right)\), the CLT result of Lemma \ref{lem:componentwise} combined with Slutsky's lemma yields the first asymptotic normality result: \begin{align*} \sqrt n(\hat\Theta_n-\Theta) &= \sqrt n D_n^{-1} D_n(\hat\Theta_n-\Theta)\\ &\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}}\mathrm{diag}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{v_1}},\ldots,\frac{1}{\sqrt{v_K}}\right) \mathcal N\!\big(0,\mathrm{diag}\left(V_1,\dots,V_K\right)\big)\\ &= \mathcal N(0,V). \end{align*} A first-order Taylor expansion of the target function around $\Theta$ gives \[ \hat\rho_n-v = G(\hat\Theta_n-\Theta) + O_p(n^{-1/2}), \] and hence \[ \sqrt n(\hat\rho_n-v)\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}}\mathcal N(0,GVG^\top). \] Finally, the bound \eqref{eq:thm-res-1} implies \[ \sqrt n\!\left(\frac{N_n}{n}-\hat\rho_n\right)=o_p(1), \] so Slutsky’s lemma yields the CLT for $\sqrt n(N_n/n-v)$ as well as the joint convergence stated in \eqref{eq:thm-res-4} and \eqref{eq:thm-res-5}.

nodes.name: alphaRTS with Forced Exploration (alphaRTS-FE)
nodes.statement: Let $h:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ a function such that \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $\lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} h(n) = +\infty$ \item $h(n)=o(\sqrt{n})$ as \(n \to +\infty\) \end{enumerate} Also we define the following sets \begin{equation} \mathbf{U}_m:=\{j\in[K]:\ N_{m,j}\le h(m)\},\qquad \mathbf{S}_m:=\arg\min_{j\in U_m} N_{m,j}. \end{equation} A design is in the \(\alpha\)RTS-FE family if its allocation probabilities obey: \begin{align} &\textbf{(Forced exploration)}\quad \mathbf{U}_m\neq\emptyset\ \Rightarrow\ \forall a\in \mathbf{S}_m:\ p_{m+1,a}=\frac{1}{|\mathbf{S}_m|}; \\ &\textbf{(Otherwise)}\quad \mathbf{U}_m=\emptyset\ \Rightarrow\ \text{$p_{m+1}$ satisfies \eqref{eq:throttle} for some $\alpha\in[0,1)$}. \end{align}

nodes.name: D-Tracking forced exploration
nodes.statement: In \cite{garivier2016optimal}, the \textit{D-Tracking} algorithm is composed of two parts, the \textit{Tracking} part as presented earlier, and the second part consists in \textit{Forced Exploration} that coincides with the \textit{\(\alpha\)RTS-FE} family with \(\alpha=0\), where they chose \(h(n) = \left(\sqrt{n} - \frac{K}{2}\right)^+.\) Note that this function doesn't verify the second condition of Definition \ref{def:rts-fe-def}. In our experiments, we use instead the function \(h(n) = \left(n^{\frac{1}{3}} - \frac{K}{2}\right)^+\) that satisfies the two conditions.

We prove in Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary2} in Appendix~\ref{appnB} that the conditions in Lemma~\ref{lem:generic-conditions-main} are valid for this new sequence $\ell_{n,k}$. The conclusion follows. nodes.name: Asymptotic chi-square distribution of the Pearson statistic
nodes.statement: Define the quantities \(S_{n,k} := N_{n,k} \hat{\theta}_{n,k}\) and \(\tilde{\theta}_n := \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} \hat{\theta}_{n,k}\). Consider a RAR procedure under which \(N_{n,k} \to +\infty\), then the Pearson Chi-square statistic \(\mathcal{X}_n := \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{\left(S_{n,k} - N_{n,k}\tilde{\theta}_n\right)^2}{N_{n,k}\tilde{\theta}_n (1 - \tilde{\theta}_n)}\) satisfies \(\mathcal{X}_n \xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} \chi^2_{K-1}\) under the null hypothesis.
assumptions: Consider a RAR procedure under which \(N_{n,k} \to +\infty\)
conclusions: \(\mathcal{X}_n \xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} \chi^2_{K-1}\)
nodes.label: lem:pearson

nodes.name: Validity of the Pearson calibration for alphaRTS(-FE)
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{lem:pearson} is valid for all \(\alpha\)RTS designs when Condition \hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}} is verified, and also for \(\alpha\)RTS-FE designs.

nodes.name: Asymptotic level of the chi-square homogeneity test
nodes.statement: Hence, the test that rejects $\mathcal{H}_0$ if $\mathcal{X}_n$ exceeds the quantile of order 0.95 of a chi-square distribution with $K-1$ degrees of freedom is asymptotically a level-$0.05$ test.
conclusions: the test that rejects $\mathcal{H}_0$ if $\mathcal{X}_n$ exceeds the quantile of order 0.95 of a chi-square distribution with $K-1$ degrees of freedom is asymptotically a level-$0.05$ test

nodes.name: RSIHR allocation
nodes.statement: RSIHR was proposed by \cite{Rosenberger01Opt}. It balances ethical and statistical considerations by minimizing the expected number of treatment failures subject to a constraint on the variance of the test statistic and is equal to \[\rho_k^R(\Theta) = \frac{\sqrt{\theta_k}}{\sum_{\ell=1}^{K}\sqrt{\theta_{\ell}}}\;.\]

nodes.name: Appendix notation: increments, Q and U
nodes.statement: We fix a design that belongs to the \(\alpha\)RTS family for some \(0\leq\alpha <1\) and introduce the following notation for \(k \in [K]\): \begin{itemize} \item $p_{m,k} = \mathbb{E}[X_{m,k} \mid \mathcal{F}_{m-1}]$ \item $\Delta M_{m,k} = X_{m,k} - \mathbb{E}[X_{m,k} \mid \mathcal{F}_{m-1}] = X_{m,k} - p_{m,k}$ \item $Q_{n,k} = \sum_{m=1}^{n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k} - \theta_{k})$ and denote \(\mathbf{Q_n} := (\mathbf{Q_{n,1}}, \dots, \mathbf{Q_{n,K}})\) \end{itemize} and \[U_{n,k} = \sum_{m=1}^{n-1} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + M_{n,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k}\;.\]

nodes.name: Last hitting time
nodes.statement: We define the last hitting time $\ell_{n,k}$ as \begin{equation} \ell_{n,k} := \max \left\{\, m \leq n ; \, \frac{N_{m,k}}{m} \leq \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \;.\right\} \end{equation}
also_stated_at: In Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary} in Appendix~\ref{appnA}, we show that these conditions are satisfied for the random sequence \[\ell_{n,k} := \max \left\{\, m \leq n ; \, \frac{N_{m,k}}{m} \leq \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \,\right\}\] for any $\alpha$RTS design. In words $\ell_{n,k}$ is the last time before \(n\) at which treatment \(k\) is under-sampled: its allocation proportion is less than or equal to the estimated target proportion.

nodes.name: Last hitting time definition
nodes.statement: \ell_{n,k} := \max \left\{\, m \leq n ; \, \frac{N_{m,k}}{m} \leq \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \;.\right\}
nodes.label: eq:stopping-time-def

nodes.name: Hitting-time conditions for alphaRTS
nodes.statement: For any \(k \in [K]\) we have the following results: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item \(\left(\ell_{n,k}\right)_{n \geq 1}\) is a non-decreasing sequence and \(\forall n \in \mathbb{N}: \,\ell_{n,k} \leq n\) \item for all $k\in [K]$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$,\begin{equation} N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq 1+N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} \end{equation} \item for all $k\in [K]$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, \begin{equation} N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq o(\sqrt{n}), \ a.s. \quad \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item \(\left(\ell_{n,k}\right)_{n \geq 1}\) is a non-decreasing sequence and \(\forall n \in \mathbb{N}: \,\ell_{n,k} \leq n\) \item for all $k\in [K]$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$,\begin{equation} N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq 1+N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} \end{equation} \item for all $k\in [K]$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, \begin{equation} N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq o(\sqrt{n}), \ a.s. \quad \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:preliminary

nodes.name: Hitting-time inequality
nodes.statement: N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq 1+N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}
nodes.label: eq:prelim-4

nodes.name: Hitting-time condition
nodes.statement: N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq o(\sqrt{n}), \ a.s. \quad
nodes.label: eq:condition

nodes.name: Proof of hitting-time conditions for alphaRTS
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Obvious from definition \eqref{eq:stopping-time-def}. \item By definition of \(U_{n,k}\) we have \(\Delta U_{m,k} = \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} - p_{m,k} + \Delta \Big( N_{m,k} - m \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \Big)\). Then \begin{align*} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &= \sum_{m=\ell_{n,k}+1}^n \Big( \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} - p_{m,k} \Big) + N_{n,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k} - \Big( N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \Big) \end{align*} So \begin{align*} N_{n,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k} &= N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + p_{\ell_{n,k}+1,k} - \alpha \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \\&\,\,+ \sum_{m=\ell_{n,k}+2}^n \underbrace{\Big( p_{m,k} - \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} \Big)}_{\leq 0 \quad} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k}, k}\\ &\leq p_{\ell_{n,k}+1,k} + N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k}, k} \end{align*} So we conclude \[N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq 1 + N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}\;.\] \item It is easy to check that if $\ell_{n,k} < K m_0+1$ then \(N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq K m_0\), and if \(\ell_{n,k} \geq Km_0 + 1\) then \(N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq 0\). So by combining the two inequalities we obtain that \(N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq K m_0 = o(\sqrt{n})\)\;. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: (i) from the definition; (ii) telescope $U$ and use the throttling rule after $\ell_{n,k}$; (iii) at $\ell_{n,k}$ the arm is under-sampled.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of the hitting time from its definition
nodes.statement: Obvious from definition \eqref{eq:stopping-time-def}.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of the hitting time from its definition

nodes.name: Telescope $U$ and use the throttling rule
nodes.statement: By definition of \(U_{n,k}\) we have \(\Delta U_{m,k} = \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} - p_{m,k} + \Delta \Big( N_{m,k} - m \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \Big)\). Then \begin{align*} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &= \sum_{m=\ell_{n,k}+1}^n \Big( \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} - p_{m,k} \Big) + N_{n,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k} - \Big( N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \Big) \end{align*} So \begin{align*} N_{n,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k} &= N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + p_{\ell_{n,k}+1,k} - \alpha \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \\&\,\,+ \sum_{m=\ell_{n,k}+2}^n \underbrace{\Big( p_{m,k} - \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} \Big)}_{\leq 0 \quad} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k}, k}\\ &\leq p_{\ell_{n,k}+1,k} + N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k}, k} \end{align*} So we conclude \[N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq 1 + N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}\;.\]
nodes.statement_short: Telescope $U$ and use the throttling rule

nodes.name: Increment of $U$
nodes.statement: By definition of \(U_{n,k}\) we have \(\Delta U_{m,k} = \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} - p_{m,k} + \Delta \Big( N_{m,k} - m \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \Big)\).
nodes.statement_short: Increment of $U$

nodes.name: Telescope from $\ell_{n,k}$ to $n$
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &= \sum_{m=\ell_{n,k}+1}^n \Big( \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} - p_{m,k} \Big) + N_{n,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k} - \Big( N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \Big) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Telescope from $\ell_{n,k}$ to $n$

nodes.name: Throttled terms are non-positive
nodes.statement: So \begin{align*} N_{n,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k} &= N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + p_{\ell_{n,k}+1,k} - \alpha \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \\&\,\,+ \sum_{m=\ell_{n,k}+2}^n \underbrace{\Big( p_{m,k} - \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m-1,k} \Big)}_{\leq 0 \quad} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k}, k}\\ &\leq p_{\ell_{n,k}+1,k} + N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k}, k} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Throttled terms are non-positive

nodes.name: Conclude inequality (ii)
nodes.statement: So we conclude \[N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \leq 1 + N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}\;.\]
nodes.statement_short: Conclude inequality (ii)

nodes.name: At the hitting time the arm is under-sampled up to the burn-
nodes.statement: It is easy to check that if $\ell_{n,k} < K m_0+1$ then \(N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq K m_0\), and if \(\ell_{n,k} \geq Km_0 + 1\) then \(N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq 0\). So by combining the two inequalities we obtain that \(N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \leq K m_0 = o(\sqrt{n})\)\;.
nodes.statement_short: At the hitting time the arm is under-sampled up to the burn-in

nodes.name: Proof of strong consistency and rates
nodes.statement: The first step of the proof, as in the work of \cite{hu2004asymptotic}, is to establish that $\hat{\rho}_{n}$ has a finite (non-sparse) limit. For \(k \in [K]\), if \(N_{n,k} \to +\infty\), then using Condition \hyperlink{CA}{\textbf{A}} and the law of large numbers we get \(\hat\theta_{n,k} \to \theta_k\). Otherwise if \(\sup_{n \geq 1}N_{n,k} < +\infty\) then \(\left(\hat\theta_{n,k}\right)_{n \geq 1}\) takes finite values and also has a limit, that belong to $V_k$ (which is defined in our statement of Condition \hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}}). Hence $\hat\theta_{n}$ converges to some element $z$ in $I_1\times \dots \times I_K$. By continuity of $\rho$ and from Condition \hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}} we obtain \begin{equation} \exists u \in (0,1)^K: \quad \hat{\rho}_n \to u:= \rho(z)\;. \end{equation} As \(M_n\) is a martingale, we have by LLN for martingales (see \cite{Chow1967}) that $M_{n,k} = o(n)$ a.s. so \begin{align*} \frac{U_{n,k}}{n} &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{m=0}^{n-1} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k} + o(1) \\ \implies \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{U_{n,k}}{n} &= - (1 - \alpha) u_k \quad a.s. \quad\text{; combining \eqref{eq:conv-rho} and the Cesaro lemma} \end{align*} Using Lemma \ref{lem:convergence} and Inequality \eqref{eq:condition} from Lemma \ref{lem:preliminary} we obtain that \[ \left(\frac{1}{n}+\frac{N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n} + \frac{U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n} \right)^+ \to 0 \quad a.s. \] So by injecting the previous result in Inequality \eqref{eq:prelim-4} from Lemma \ref{lem:preliminary}, we obtain \[ \forall k \in [K]: \, \left(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}\right)^+ \to 0 \quad a.s. \] and we have \begin{align*} \left(\hat{\rho}_{n,k} - \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\right)^+ &= \left(1 - \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - (1 - \hat{\rho}_{n,k})\right)^+ \\ &= \left(\sum_{j=1; j \neq k}^K \frac{N_{n,j}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,j}\right)^+ \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1; j \neq k}^K \left(\frac{N_{n,j}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,j}\right)^+ \to 0 \end{align*} So we obtain that \(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k} \to 0\), and then \(\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \hat{\rho}_{n,k} = u_k \in (0,1)\) A straightforward consequence is that $\forall k \in [K], N_{n,k} \to \infty$ a.s., hence $\hat{\Theta}_n \to \Theta$ and by continuity of \(\rho\) we obtain that \(\hat{\rho}_n = \rho(\hat{\Theta}_n) \to \rho(\Theta) = v \in (0,1)^K\), hence \[ \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} = \lim_{n \to \infty} \hat{\rho}_{n,k} = v_k \] Using further Lemma A.4 \cite{hu2004asymptotic} and the Law of Iterated Logarithm we get \[ \hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log\!\log n}{n}}\right) \quad \text{a.s.} \] In addition, the second order Taylor expansion of \(\rho\) gives that \begin{align*} \hat{\rho}_n - v &= (\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O(\|\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta\|^2) \\ &= O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log\!\log n}{n}}\right) \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Show $\hat\rho_n$ has a non-sparse limit, use the martingale LLN for $U_{n,k}/n$ and Lemma C.5 to get $N_n/n-\hat\rho_n\to0$; rates from the LIL and Taylor expansion.

nodes.name: Goal: non-sparse limit of $\hat\rho_n$
nodes.statement: The first step of the proof, as in the work of \cite{hu2004asymptotic}, is to establish that $\hat{\rho}_{n}$ has a finite (non-sparse) limit.
nodes.statement_short: Goal: non-sparse limit of $\hat\rho_n$

nodes.name: Estimators converge whether or not each arm is sampled infin
nodes.statement: For \(k \in [K]\), if \(N_{n,k} \to +\infty\), then using Condition \hyperlink{CA}{\textbf{A}} and the law of large numbers we get \(\hat\theta_{n,k} \to \theta_k\). Otherwise if \(\sup_{n \geq 1}N_{n,k} < +\infty\) then \(\left(\hat\theta_{n,k}\right)_{n \geq 1}\) takes finite values and also has a limit, that belong to $V_k$ (which is defined in our statement of Condition \hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}}). Hence $\hat\theta_{n}$ converges to some element $z$ in $I_1\times \dots \times I_K$.
nodes.statement_short: Estimators converge whether or not each arm is sampled infinitely often

nodes.name: Continuity and Condition B give a limit $u\in(0,1)^K$
nodes.statement: By continuity of $\rho$ and from Condition \hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}} we obtain \begin{equation} \exists u \in (0,1)^K: \quad \hat{\rho}_n \to u:= \rho(z)\;. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Continuity and Condition B give a limit $u\in(0,1)^K$

nodes.name: Convergence of plug-in target
nodes.statement: \exists u \in (0,1)^K: \quad \hat{\rho}_n \to u:= \rho(z)\;.
nodes.label: eq:conv-rho

nodes.name: Martingale LLN and Cesaro give $U_{n,k}/n\to-(1-\alpha)u_k$
nodes.statement: As \(M_n\) is a martingale, we have by LLN for martingales (see \cite{Chow1967}) that $M_{n,k} = o(n)$ a.s. so \begin{align*} \frac{U_{n,k}}{n} &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{m=0}^{n-1} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k} + o(1) \\ \implies \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{U_{n,k}}{n} &= - (1 - \alpha) u_k \quad a.s. \quad\text{; combining \eqref{eq:conv-rho} and the Cesaro lemma} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Martingale LLN and Cesaro give $U_{n,k}/n\to-(1-\alpha)u_k$

nodes.name: Lemma C.5 makes the bound vanish
nodes.statement: Using Lemma \ref{lem:convergence} and Inequality \eqref{eq:condition} from Lemma \ref{lem:preliminary} we obtain that \[ \left(\frac{1}{n}+\frac{N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n} + \frac{U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n} \right)^+ \to 0 \quad a.s. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.5 makes the bound vanish

nodes.name: Positive parts of the tracking errors vanish in both directi
nodes.statement: So by injecting the previous result in Inequality \eqref{eq:prelim-4} from Lemma \ref{lem:preliminary}, we obtain \[ \forall k \in [K]: \, \left(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}\right)^+ \to 0 \quad a.s. \] and we have \begin{align*} \left(\hat{\rho}_{n,k} - \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\right)^+ &= \left(1 - \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - (1 - \hat{\rho}_{n,k})\right)^+ \\ &= \left(\sum_{j=1; j \neq k}^K \frac{N_{n,j}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,j}\right)^+ \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1; j \neq k}^K \left(\frac{N_{n,j}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,j}\right)^+ \to 0 \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Positive parts of the tracking errors vanish in both directions

nodes.name: Conclude $N_n/n\to v$
nodes.statement: So we obtain that \(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k} \to 0\), and then \(\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \hat{\rho}_{n,k} = u_k \in (0,1)\) A straightforward consequence is that $\forall k \in [K], N_{n,k} \to \infty$ a.s., hence $\hat{\Theta}_n \to \Theta$ and by continuity of \(\rho\) we obtain that \(\hat{\rho}_n = \rho(\hat{\Theta}_n) \to \rho(\Theta) = v \in (0,1)^K\), hence \[ \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} = \lim_{n \to \infty} \hat{\rho}_{n,k} = v_k \]
nodes.statement_short: Conclude $N_n/n\to v$

nodes.name: LIL rate for $\hat\Theta_n$
nodes.statement: Using further Lemma A.4 \cite{hu2004asymptotic} and the Law of Iterated Logarithm we get \[ \hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log\!\log n}{n}}\right) \quad \text{a.s.} \]
nodes.statement_short: LIL rate for $\hat\Theta_n$

nodes.name: Taylor expansion transfers the rate to $\hat\rho_n$
nodes.statement: In addition, the second order Taylor expansion of \(\rho\) gives that \begin{align*} \hat{\rho}_n - v &= (\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O(\|\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta\|^2) \\ &= O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log\!\log n}{n}}\right) \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansion transfers the rate to $\hat\rho_n$

nodes.name: Increment decomposition of U
nodes.statement: Let $(\ell_n)_{n \geq 1}$ a positive increasing sequence such that $\forall n \in \mathbb{N}: \ell_n \leq n$. Under conditions \hyperlink{CA}{\textbf{A}} and \hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}} we have the following \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For all \(k \in [K]\) \begin{equation} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n},k} = (n - \ell_{n})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n},k} + \ell_{n} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}) \end{equation} \item There exists a constant \(C \geq 0\) such that \begin{equation} |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_n - \hat{\rho}_{\ell_n})| \le o(1)(n-\ell_n) + C\|Q_n - Q_{\ell_n}\| + o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let $(\ell_n)_{n \geq 1}$ a positive increasing sequence such that $\forall n \in \mathbb{N}: \ell_n \leq n$.
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For all \(k \in [K]\) \begin{equation} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n},k} = (n - \ell_{n})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n},k} + \ell_{n} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}) \end{equation} \item There exists a constant \(C \geq 0\) such that \begin{equation} |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_n - \hat{\rho}_{\ell_n})| \le o(1)(n-\ell_n) + C\|Q_n - Q_{\ell_n}\| + o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:diff-U-approx

nodes.name: Decomposition of U increments
nodes.statement: U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n},k} = (n - \ell_{n})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n},k} + \ell_{n} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k})
nodes.label: eq:prelim-2

nodes.name: Bound on plug-in target increments
nodes.statement: |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_n - \hat{\rho}_{\ell_n})| \le o(1)(n-\ell_n) + C\|Q_n - Q_{\ell_n}\| + o_p(\sqrt{n})

nodes.name: Proof of the increment decomposition of U
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item \begin{align*} &U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n},k} = \sum_{m=\ell_{n}}^{n-1} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k} - n \hat{\rho}_{n,k} + \ell_{n} \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n},k} + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k} \\ =& \sum_{m=\ell_{n}}^{n-1} \alpha (\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - v_k) + \alpha(n - \ell_{n}) v_k - (n - \ell_{n}) \hat{\rho}_{n,k} + \ell_{n} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}) \\ &\quad + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n},k} \\ =& -(1 - \alpha)(n - \ell_{n}) v_k + \sum_{m=\ell_{n}}^{n-1} \alpha (\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - v_k) - (n - \ell_{n})(\hat{\rho}_{n,k} - v_k) + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n},k} \\ &\quad + \ell_{n} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}) \\ =& (n-\ell_{n})\left[-(1 - \alpha)v_k - (\hat{\rho}_{n,k} - v_k) + \frac{\alpha}{n - \ell_{n}}\sum_{m=\ell_{n}}^{n-1} (\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - v_k)\right]+ M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n},k} \\ &\quad + \ell_{n} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}) \\ \end{align*} Theorem \ref{thm:LLN} applies here and gives that \(\lim_{n \to +\infty} \hat{\rho}_n = v\). If \(\left(\ell_{n}\right)_{n \geq 1}\) is bounded then it is stationary, so the Cesaro yields \(\frac{1}{n - \ell_{n}}\sum_{m=\ell_{n}}^{n-1} (\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - v_k) = o(1)\). Otherwise if \(\ell_{n} \to +\infty\), we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{n - \ell_{n}}\left|\sum_{m=\ell_{n}}^{n-1} \hat{\rho}_{m,k} - v_k\right| &\leq \frac{1}{n - \ell_{n}}\sum_{m=\ell_{n}}^{n-1} |\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - v_k| \\ &\leq \sup_{\ell_{n} \leq m \leq n}|\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - v_k| \to 0\;. \end{align*} In both cases we obtain \begin{equation*} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n},k} = (n - \ell_{n})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n},k} + \ell_{n} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}) \end{equation*} \item Let \( D_{n,k} := \sum_{j=1}^{n} X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k) \), then using Lemma \ref{lem:chebychev-mart} we have for \( M>0 \) \begin{align*} \sup_{n\geq 1} \mathbb{P}(D_{n,k} > M\sqrt{n}) &\leq \sup_{n\geq 1} \mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{1\leq i\leq n} D_{i,k} \geq M\sqrt{n}\right) \\ &\leq \sup_{n\geq 1} \frac{\mathbb{V}ar\left[D_{n,k}\right]} {\mathbb{V}ar\left[D_{n,k}\right] + M^2 n} \\ &\leq \frac{\mathbb{V}ar[\xi_{1,k}]} {\mathbb{V}ar[\xi_{1,k}] + M^2}. \end{align*} It follows that \( D_{n,k} = O_p(\sqrt{n}) \). Moreover, we have \(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{N_{n,k}} =\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\frac{n}{N_{n,k}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} O_p(1) = O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\) and \(N_{n,k}^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sqrt{n}N_{n,k}^{-1/2} = O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\). Using the Bahadur representation of the estimator in \eqref{eq:bahadur-estimator} we obtain \begin{align*} \hat{\theta}_{n,k} - \theta_k &= \frac{D_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}} + o_p\!\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right) \\ &= O_p\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{N_{n,k}}\right) + o_p\!\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right) \\ &= O_p\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right) + o_p\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\\ &= O_p\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right). \end{align*} So the second order Taylor expansion of \(\rho\) gives \begin{align} \hat{\rho}_n - v &= (\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O(\|\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta\|^2) \\ &= (\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O_p\left(\frac{1}{n}\right) \end{align} Similarly we obtain \( \hat{\rho}_{\ell_n} - v = (\hat{\Theta}_{\ell_n}-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O_p\left(\frac{1}{\ell_n}\right) \). Combining the two previous equations gives \begin{eqnarray*} \ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n) = \ell_n(\hat{\Theta}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\Theta}_n)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + \left(O_p\left(\frac{\ell_n}{n}\right)+O_p(1)\right) \\ \implies |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)| \le C \ell_n \|\hat{\Theta}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\Theta}_n\| + O_p(1) \end{eqnarray*} And we have \begin{align*} \hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\hat{\theta}_{\ell_n,k} &= \frac{1}{N_{n,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)-\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{\ell_n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\\ &= \frac{1}{N_{n,k}}\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^{n} X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k) + \left(\frac{1}{N_{n,k}} - \frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\right)\sum_{j=1}^{\ell_n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\\[8pt] &= \frac{1}{N_{n,k}}\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^{n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k) + \frac{N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}}\cdot\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{\ell_n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\\[8pt] &\quad +\, o\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right) + o\left(N_{\ell_n,k}^{-1/2}\right) \end{align*} So \begin{align*} |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)| &\le C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^{n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\right\|\\ &\quad + C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n|N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}|}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{\ell_n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\right\|\\ &\quad + \ell_n \cdot o\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right) + \ell_n \cdot o\left(N_{\ell_n,k}^{-1/2}\right) \end{align*} And for some two sequences $a_n$ and $b_n$ converging to $0$ as $n \to + \infty$ \begin{align*} \ell_n\cdot o\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right)+\ell_n\cdot o\left(N_{\ell_n,k}^{-1/2}\right) &= \ell_n\,N_{n,k}^{-1/2}a_n + \ell_n \,N_{\ell_n,k}^{-1/2}b_n\\ &= \sqrt{n}\left(\frac{\ell_n}{n}\left(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}a_{n} + \sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n}}\left(\frac{N_{\ell_n,k}}{\ell_n}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}b_{n}\right)\\ &= o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{align*} as \quad \(\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty} \frac{\ell_n}{n}\left(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\right)^{-1/2}a_n + \sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n}}\left(\frac{N_{\ell_n,k}}{\ell_n}\right)^{-1/2}b_n=0\)\;. Since \(\ell_n \le n\) and \(\frac{n}{N_{n,k}}\to v_k^{-1}\) we have \begin{align*} C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\sum_{m=\ell_n+1}^{n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| &=C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n}{n}\frac{n}{N_{n,k}}\|Q_{n,k}-Q_{\ell_n,k}\|\\ &\le C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|Q_{n,k}-Q_{\ell_n,k}\|\\ &= C\|Q_n-Q_{\ell_n}\| \end{align*} On the second part of the inequality we use that \(N_{n,k} - N_{\ell_{n}, k} \leq n - \ell_n\): \begin{align*} &C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n|N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}|}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\|\\&= C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n|N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}|}{N_{\ell_n,k}N_{n,k}}\left\|\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\|\\ & \leq C(n-\ell_n) \sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\frac{n}{N_{n,k}} \left\|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| \end{align*} If \((\ell_{n})_{n\geq1}\) is bounded, then \(\frac{1}{n}\left\|\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| = o(1)\). Otherwise if \(\ell_n \to +\infty\) then we can use the argument of \cite{Doob1936} and conclude that \[\frac{1}{\ell_n}\left\|\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| = o(1)\] Combined with the fact that \(N_{n,k} \sim v_k.n\), we obtain that \begin{align*} \frac{\ell_n}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\frac{n}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| = o(1) \end{align*} So \begin{equation*} C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n|N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}|}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| \leq (n-\ell_n) o(1) \end{equation*} Combining the previous results we obtain \[ |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_n - \hat{\rho}_{\ell_n})| \le o(1)(n-\ell_n) + C\|Q_n - Q_{\ell_n}\| + o_p(\sqrt{n}) \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: (i) algebraic rewriting plus Cesaro; (ii) Taylor-expand $\rho$ and bound estimator increments via martingale maximal inequalities.

nodes.statement_short: Prove the plug-in increment bound (ii)

nodes.name: Maximal inequality bound on $D_{n,k}$
nodes.statement: Let \( D_{n,k} := \sum_{j=1}^{n} X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k) \), then using Lemma \ref{lem:chebychev-mart} we have for \( M>0 \) \begin{align*} \sup_{n\geq 1} \mathbb{P}(D_{n,k} > M\sqrt{n}) &\leq \sup_{n\geq 1} \mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{1\leq i\leq n} D_{i,k} \geq M\sqrt{n}\right) \\ &\leq \sup_{n\geq 1} \frac{\mathbb{V}ar\left[D_{n,k}\right]} {\mathbb{V}ar\left[D_{n,k}\right] + M^2 n} \\ &\leq \frac{\mathbb{V}ar[\xi_{1,k}]} {\mathbb{V}ar[\xi_{1,k}] + M^2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Maximal inequality bound on $D_{n,k}$

nodes.name: Orders of $D_{n,k}$ and $N_{n,k}^{-1/2}$
nodes.statement: It follows that \( D_{n,k} = O_p(\sqrt{n}) \). Moreover, we have \(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{N_{n,k}} =\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\frac{n}{N_{n,k}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} O_p(1) = O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\) and \(N_{n,k}^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sqrt{n}N_{n,k}^{-1/2} = O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\).
nodes.statement_short: Orders of $D_{n,k}$ and $N_{n,k}^{-1/2}$

nodes.name: Estimator error is $O_p(n^{-1/2})$
nodes.statement: Using the Bahadur representation of the estimator in \eqref{eq:bahadur-estimator} we obtain \begin{align*} \hat{\theta}_{n,k} - \theta_k &= \frac{D_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}} + o_p\!\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right) \\ &= O_p\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{N_{n,k}}\right) + o_p\!\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right) \\ &= O_p\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right) + o_p\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\\ &= O_p\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Estimator error is $O_p(n^{-1/2})$

nodes.name: Taylor expansions of $\hat\rho_n$ and $\hat\rho_{\ell_n}$
nodes.statement: So the second order Taylor expansion of \(\rho\) gives \begin{align} \hat{\rho}_n - v &= (\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O(\|\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta\|^2) \\ &= (\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O_p\left(\frac{1}{n}\right) \end{align} Similarly we obtain \( \hat{\rho}_{\ell_n} - v = (\hat{\Theta}_{\ell_n}-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O_p\left(\frac{1}{\ell_n}\right) \).
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansions of $\hat\rho_n$ and $\hat\rho_{\ell_n}$

nodes.name: First-order expansion of plug-in target
nodes.statement: \hat{\rho}_n - v &= (\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O(\|\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta\|^2) \\ &= (\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + O_p\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)
nodes.label: eq:approx-rho-Op

nodes.name: Bound the plug-in difference by the estimator difference
nodes.statement: Combining the two previous equations gives \begin{eqnarray*} \ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n) = \ell_n(\hat{\Theta}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\Theta}_n)\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial y}\Big|_{\Theta} + \left(O_p\left(\frac{\ell_n}{n}\right)+O_p(1)\right) \\ \implies |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)| \le C \ell_n \|\hat{\Theta}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\Theta}_n\| + O_p(1) \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the plug-in difference by the estimator difference

nodes.name: Decompose the estimator difference
nodes.statement: And we have \begin{align*} \hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\hat{\theta}_{\ell_n,k} &= \frac{1}{N_{n,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)-\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{\ell_n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\\ &= \frac{1}{N_{n,k}}\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^{n} X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k) + \left(\frac{1}{N_{n,k}} - \frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\right)\sum_{j=1}^{\ell_n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\\[8pt] &= \frac{1}{N_{n,k}}\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^{n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k) + \frac{N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}}\cdot\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{\ell_n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\\[8pt] &\quad +\, o\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right) + o\left(N_{\ell_n,k}^{-1/2}\right) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the estimator difference

nodes.name: Three-term bound
nodes.statement: So \begin{align*} |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)| &\le C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^{n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\right\|\\ &\quad + C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n|N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}|}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{j=1}^{\ell_n}X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k)\right\|\\ &\quad + \ell_n \cdot o\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right) + \ell_n \cdot o\left(N_{\ell_n,k}^{-1/2}\right) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Three-term bound

nodes.name: Remainder terms are $o_p(\sqrt n)$
nodes.statement: And for some two sequences $a_n$ and $b_n$ converging to $0$ as $n \to + \infty$ \begin{align*} \ell_n\cdot o\left(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}\right)+\ell_n\cdot o\left(N_{\ell_n,k}^{-1/2}\right) &= \ell_n\,N_{n,k}^{-1/2}a_n + \ell_n \,N_{\ell_n,k}^{-1/2}b_n\\ &= \sqrt{n}\left(\frac{\ell_n}{n}\left(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}a_{n} + \sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n}}\left(\frac{N_{\ell_n,k}}{\ell_n}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}b_{n}\right)\\ &= o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{align*} as \quad \(\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty} \frac{\ell_n}{n}\left(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\right)^{-1/2}a_n + \sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n}}\left(\frac{N_{\ell_n,k}}{\ell_n}\right)^{-1/2}b_n=0\)\;.
nodes.statement_short: Remainder terms are $o_p(\sqrt n)$

nodes.name: First term bounded by $C\|Q_n-Q_{\ell_n}\|$
nodes.statement: Since \(\ell_n \le n\) and \(\frac{n}{N_{n,k}}\to v_k^{-1}\) we have \begin{align*} C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\sum_{m=\ell_n+1}^{n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| &=C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n}{n}\frac{n}{N_{n,k}}\|Q_{n,k}-Q_{\ell_n,k}\|\\ &\le C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|Q_{n,k}-Q_{\ell_n,k}\|\\ &= C\|Q_n-Q_{\ell_n}\| \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: First term bounded by $C\|Q_n-Q_{\ell_n}\|$

nodes.name: Second term bounded using $N_{n,k}-N_{\ell_n,k}\le n-\ell_n$
nodes.statement: On the second part of the inequality we use that \(N_{n,k} - N_{\ell_{n}, k} \leq n - \ell_n\): \begin{align*} &C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n|N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}|}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\|\\&= C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n|N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}|}{N_{\ell_n,k}N_{n,k}}\left\|\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\|\\ & \leq C(n-\ell_n) \sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\frac{n}{N_{n,k}} \left\|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Second term bounded using $N_{n,k}-N_{\ell_n,k}\le n-\ell_n$

nodes.name: Bounded hitting times
nodes.statement: If \((\ell_{n})_{n\geq1}\) is bounded, then \(\frac{1}{n}\left\|\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| = o(1)\).
nodes.statement_short: Bounded hitting times

nodes.name: Unbounded hitting times: Doob's argument
nodes.statement: Otherwise if \(\ell_n \to +\infty\) then we can use the argument of \cite{Doob1936} and conclude that \[\frac{1}{\ell_n}\left\|\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| = o(1)\]
nodes.statement_short: Unbounded hitting times: Doob's argument

nodes.name: Second term is $(n-\ell_n)o(1)$
nodes.statement: Combined with the fact that \(N_{n,k} \sim v_k.n\), we obtain that \begin{align*} \frac{\ell_n}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\frac{n}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| = o(1) \end{align*} So \begin{equation*} C\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\ell_n|N_{\ell_n,k}-N_{n,k}|}{N_{n,k}}\left\|\frac{1}{N_{\ell_n,k}}\sum_{m=1}^{\ell_n}X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)\right\| \leq (n-\ell_n) o(1) \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Second term is $(n-\ell_n)o(1)$

nodes.name: Conclude (ii)
nodes.statement: Combining the previous results we obtain \[ |\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_n - \hat{\rho}_{\ell_n})| \le o(1)(n-\ell_n) + C\|Q_n - Q_{\ell_n}\| + o_p(\sqrt{n}) \]
nodes.statement_short: Conclude (ii)

nodes.name: Upper bounds on U increments
nodes.statement: Under conditions \hyperlink{CA}{\textbf{A}}--\hyperlink{CB}{\textbf{B}} , we have for every \(k \in [K]\) as \(n \to +\infty\) \begin{align} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &\leq o_p(\sqrt{n}) \\ U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &\leq O(\sqrt{n \log \log(n)}) \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align}
conclusions: \begin{align} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &\leq o_p(\sqrt{n}) \\ U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &\leq O(\sqrt{n \log \log(n)}) \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align}
nodes.label: lem:U-ineq

nodes.name: U increment o_P bound
nodes.statement: U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &\leq o_p(\sqrt{n})
nodes.label: eq:ineq-U-1

nodes.name: U increment LIL bound
nodes.statement: U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &\leq O(\sqrt{n \log \log(n)}) \quad \text{a.s.}
nodes.label: eq:ineq-U-2

nodes.name: Proof of upper bounds on U increments
nodes.statement: Let \((L_n)_{n \geq 1}\) a positive sequence such that $L_n \to \infty$ and $L_n = o(n)$. From Lemma \ref{lem:mart-1} we have \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E}\left[\max_{m \leq L_n} \|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\| \right] \leq 2\sqrt{L_n C_0} \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{E}\left[\max_{L_n \leq m < n} \frac{\|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\|}{m} \right] \leq 3\sqrt{\frac{C_0}{L_n}} \end{equation*} Applying Lemma \ref{lem:expectation-to-O} we obtain, \begin{align*} \max_{L_n \leq m < n} \frac{\|Q_m - Q_{n-m}\|}{m} &= O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{L_n}}\right) = o_p(1)\\ \max_{L_n \leq m < n} \|Q_m - Q_{n-m}\| &= O_p(\sqrt{L_n}) \leq o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{align*} From Lemma \ref{lem:mart-2}, we have that for all \(L < n\): \begin{equation} \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| \leq (n - \ell_{n,k}) \max_{L \leq m < n} \frac{\|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\|}{m} + \max_{m < L} \|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\| \end{equation} So using \eqref{eq:ineq-proof-1}, and applying the same steps on the martingale \(\{M_n\}_{n \geq 1}\), we obtain \begin{equation} \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| \leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n}), \quad |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| \leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{equation} From inequality \eqref{eq:prelim-22} of Lemma \ref{lem:diff-U-approx} and \eqref{eq:ineq-M-U} \begin{align} |\ell_{n,k} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k})| &\leq o(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + C \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| + o_p(\sqrt{n})\notag\\ &\leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{align} As \(\left(\ell_{n,k}\right)_{n \geq 0}\) is a non-decreasing sequence of positive integers, and that \(\ell_{n,k} \leq n\), we can apply \eqref{eq:prelim-2} of Lemma \ref{lem:diff-U-approx} and we get \begin{align*} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &= (n - \ell_{n,k})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k} + \ell_{n,k} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k})\\ &\leq (n - \ell_{n,k})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| + \ell_{n,k} |\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}|\\ &= (n - \ell_{n,k})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o_p(1)] + o_p(\sqrt{n})\\ &\leq o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{align*} Which prove \eqref{eq:ineq-U-1}. For the second inequality, we proved in Theorem \ref{thm:LLN} that \(n(\hat{\rho}_n - v) = O\left(\sqrt{n \log \log n}\right) \quad \text{a.s.}\) which also gives that \begin{align*} \ell_{n,k}(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}) &= O\left(\sqrt{n \log \log n}\right) + O\left(\sqrt{\ell_{n,k} \log \log \ell_{n,k}}\right) \\ &= O\left(\sqrt{n \log \log n}\right) \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align*} Also, $\{M_{n,k}\}_{n \geq 1}$ is a martingale, so by LIL for martingales (see \cite{Stout1970}) we have \(M_{n,k} = O\left(\sqrt{n \log\!\log n}\right)\) then \begin{align*} M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k} &= O\left(\sqrt{n \log\!\log n}\right) + O\left(\sqrt{\ell_{n,k} \log\!\log \ell_{n,k}}\right)\\ &= O\left(\sqrt{n \log\!\log n}\right) \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align*} So we obtain the second inequality \eqref{eq:ineq-U-2} \begin{align*} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &\leq (n - \ell_{n,k})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| + \ell_{n,k} |\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}|\\ &\leq O\left(\sqrt{n \log \log n}\right) \quad a.s. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Control martingale increments with Lemmas C.1, C.2 and C.6, plug into Lemma A.2; the a.s. bound uses the LIL for martingales.

nodes.name: Lemma C.1 bounds martingale increments in expectation
nodes.statement: Let \((L_n)_{n \geq 1}\) a positive sequence such that $L_n \to \infty$ and $L_n = o(n)$. From Lemma \ref{lem:mart-1} we have \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E}\left[\max_{m \leq L_n} \|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\| \right] \leq 2\sqrt{L_n C_0} \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{E}\left[\max_{L_n \leq m < n} \frac{\|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\|}{m} \right] \leq 3\sqrt{\frac{C_0}{L_n}} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.1 bounds martingale increments in expectation

nodes.name: Lemma C.2 converts to $O_p$ bounds
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma \ref{lem:expectation-to-O} we obtain, \begin{align*} \max_{L_n \leq m < n} \frac{\|Q_m - Q_{n-m}\|}{m} &= O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{L_n}}\right) = o_p(1)\\ \max_{L_n \leq m < n} \|Q_m - Q_{n-m}\| &= O_p(\sqrt{L_n}) \leq o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.2 converts to $O_p$ bounds

nodes.name: Lemma C.6 splits the increment
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lem:mart-2}, we have that for all \(L < n\): \begin{equation} \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| \leq (n - \ell_{n,k}) \max_{L \leq m < n} \frac{\|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\|}{m} + \max_{m < L} \|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\| \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.6 splits the increment

nodes.name: Increment splitting
nodes.statement: \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| \leq (n - \ell_{n,k}) \max_{L \leq m < n} \frac{\|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\|}{m} + \max_{m < L} \|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\|
nodes.label: eq:ineq-proof-1

nodes.name: Bounds for $Q$ and $M$ increments
nodes.statement: So using \eqref{eq:ineq-proof-1}, and applying the same steps on the martingale \(\{M_n\}_{n \geq 1}\), we obtain \begin{equation} \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| \leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n}), \quad |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| \leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bounds for $Q$ and $M$ increments

nodes.name: Martingale increment bounds
nodes.statement: \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| \leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n}), \quad |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| \leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n})
nodes.label: eq:ineq-M-U

nodes.name: Lemma A.2 (ii) bounds the plug-in increment
nodes.statement: From inequality \eqref{eq:prelim-22} of Lemma \ref{lem:diff-U-approx} and \eqref{eq:ineq-M-U} \begin{align} |\ell_{n,k} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k})| &\leq o(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + C \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| + o_p(\sqrt{n})\notag\\ &\leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma A.2 (ii) bounds the plug-in increment

nodes.name: Plug-in increment bound
nodes.statement: |\ell_{n,k} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k})| &\leq o(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + C \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| + o_p(\sqrt{n})\notag\\ &\leq o_p(1)(n - \ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt{n})
nodes.label: eq:ineq_ell

nodes.name: Lemma A.2 (i) gives the $o_p$ bound
nodes.statement: As \(\left(\ell_{n,k}\right)_{n \geq 0}\) is a non-decreasing sequence of positive integers, and that \(\ell_{n,k} \leq n\), we can apply \eqref{eq:prelim-2} of Lemma \ref{lem:diff-U-approx} and we get \begin{align*} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &= (n - \ell_{n,k})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k} + \ell_{n,k} (\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k})\\ &\leq (n - \ell_{n,k})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| + \ell_{n,k} |\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}|\\ &= (n - \ell_{n,k})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o_p(1)] + o_p(\sqrt{n})\\ &\leq o_p(\sqrt{n}) \end{align*} Which prove \eqref{eq:ineq-U-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma A.2 (i) gives the $o_p$ bound

nodes.name: Theorem 4.1 rate for plug-in increments
nodes.statement: For the second inequality, we proved in Theorem \ref{thm:LLN} that \(n(\hat{\rho}_n - v) = O\left(\sqrt{n \log \log n}\right) \quad \text{a.s.}\) which also gives that \begin{align*} \ell_{n,k}(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}) &= O\left(\sqrt{n \log \log n}\right) + O\left(\sqrt{\ell_{n,k} \log \log \ell_{n,k}}\right) \\ &= O\left(\sqrt{n \log \log n}\right) \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 4.1 rate for plug-in increments

nodes.name: LIL for martingales
nodes.statement: Also, $\{M_{n,k}\}_{n \geq 1}$ is a martingale, so by LIL for martingales (see \cite{Stout1970}) we have \(M_{n,k} = O\left(\sqrt{n \log\!\log n}\right)\) then \begin{align*} M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k} &= O\left(\sqrt{n \log\!\log n}\right) + O\left(\sqrt{\ell_{n,k} \log\!\log \ell_{n,k}}\right)\\ &= O\left(\sqrt{n \log\!\log n}\right) \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: LIL for martingales

nodes.name: Conclude the a.s. bound
nodes.statement: So we obtain the second inequality \eqref{eq:ineq-U-2} \begin{align*} U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} &\leq (n - \ell_{n,k})[-(1 - \alpha)v_k + o(1)] + |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| + \ell_{n,k} |\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}|\\ &\leq O\left(\sqrt{n \log \log n}\right) \quad a.s. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the a.s. bound

nodes.name: Proof of the componentwise joint CLT
nodes.statement: This proof is based on the central limit theorem for martingales. \textbf{Step 1. Defining the martingale.} For \(k \in [K]\) we define \( Y_{i,k} = \xi_{i,k} - \theta_k \) and \(M_{n,k} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} X_{i,k} Y_{i,k}.\) So \(\{M_{n,k}\}_{n \geq 0}\) is a martingale as we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\Delta M_{i,k} \mid \mathcal{F}_{i-1}] &= \mathbb{E}[M_{i,k} - M_{i-1,k} \mid \mathcal{F}_{i-1}]\\ &= \mathbb{E}[X_{i,k} Y_{i,k} \mid \mathcal{F}_{i-1}]\\ &= X_{i,k} \, \mathbb{E}[Y_{i,k}]\\ &= 0 \end{align*} The quadratic variation of \( \{M_{n,k}\}_{n \geq 0} \) can be expressed as: \begin{align*} \langle M_{.,k} \rangle_n &= \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathbb{E}\left[ (\Delta M_i)^2 \mid \mathcal{F}_{i-1} \right]\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathbb{E}\left[ X_{i,k} Y_{i,k}^2 \mid \mathcal{F}_{i-1} \right]\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^{n} X_{i,k}\mathbb{E}\left[Y_{i,k}^2 \mid \mathcal{F}_{i-1} \right]\\ &= V_k N_{n,k} \end{align*} And for \(k \neq j \in [K]\) we have \[ \left<M_{.,k}, M_{.,j}\right>_n = \sum_{s=1}^{n} \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\xi_{s,k} - \theta_{k}\right)\left(\xi_{s,j} - \theta_{j}\right)\underbrace{X_{s,k}X_{s,j}}_{= 0}\mid \mathcal{F}_{s-1}\right] = 0\] \textbf{Step 2. nodes.name: Proof of consistency and rate for sparse targets
nodes.statement: We first prove that \(N_{n,k} \to +\infty\). Let us assume towards contradiction that \[ \exists i \in [K],\ \exists M \in \mathbb{N},\ \exists N \in \mathbb{N}: \, \forall n \geq N:\ N_{n,i} = M \] As \(h(n) \to +\infty\) we can select \(N\) such that \(\forall n \geq N: \, h(n) \geq M \). Now consider \( n \geq N \), we have \begin{align*} N_{n,i} \leq h(n) & \Rightarrow \ i \in U_n \\ & \Rightarrow U_n \neq \emptyset \\ & \Rightarrow I_{n+1} \in \arg\min_{j \in U_n} N_j(n) \\ & \Rightarrow N_{n, I_{n+1}} \leq N_{n,i} = M \end{align*} Since \( I_{n+1} \) has been selected at round \( n+1 \), we have \(N_{n+1, I_{n+1}} = N_{n, I_{n+1}} + 1 \leq M + 1\), and for \( j \neq I_{n+1} \) we have \(N_{n+1,j} = N_{n,j}\). Now define \(D(n) := \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_j(n)\right)^+\), then we have \begin{align*} D(n+1) - D(n) &= \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_{n+1, j}\right)^+ - \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_{n,j}\right)^+ \\ &= \left(M + 1 - N_{n+1, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ - \left(M + 1 - N_{n, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ \\ &= \left(M - N_{n, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ - \left(M - N_{n, I_{n+1}} + 1\right)^+ \\ &= -1. \end{align*} Thus \(D\left(n + D(n) + 1\right) = -1\) which is a contradiction as \(D \geq 0\). Therefore, \[ \forall i \in [K], \quad N_{n,i} \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} +\infty. \] From the result above we have that \(\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k \to 0\) using the law of large numbers. Additionally, by using the Law of Iterated Logarithm for martingales we obtain that \[\hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log\log(N_{n,k})}{N_{n,k}}}\right) \quad a.s.\] In the same spirit of the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:LLN}, we use the continuity of \(\rho\) and Lemma \ref{lem:convergence} to obtain that \(\lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} = \lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} \hat{\rho}_{n,k} = v_k\)
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction via the potential $D(n)$ shows every arm is sampled infinitely often; then LLN, LIL and Lemma C.5.

nodes.name: Claim: every arm is sampled infinitely often
nodes.statement: We first prove that \(N_{n,k} \to +\infty\). Let us assume towards contradiction that \[ \exists i \in [K],\ \exists M \in \mathbb{N},\ \exists N \in \mathbb{N}: \, \forall n \geq N:\ N_{n,i} = M \] As \(h(n) \to +\infty\) we can select \(N\) such that \(\forall n \geq N: \, h(n) \geq M \). Now consider \( n \geq N \), we have \begin{align*} N_{n,i} \leq h(n) & \Rightarrow \ i \in U_n \\ & \Rightarrow U_n \neq \emptyset \\ & \Rightarrow I_{n+1} \in \arg\min_{j \in U_n} N_j(n) \\ & \Rightarrow N_{n, I_{n+1}} \leq N_{n,i} = M \end{align*} Since \( I_{n+1} \) has been selected at round \( n+1 \), we have \(N_{n+1, I_{n+1}} = N_{n, I_{n+1}} + 1 \leq M + 1\), and for \( j \neq I_{n+1} \) we have \(N_{n+1,j} = N_{n,j}\). Now define \(D(n) := \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_j(n)\right)^+\), then we have \begin{align*} D(n+1) - D(n) &= \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_{n+1, j}\right)^+ - \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_{n,j}\right)^+ \\ &= \left(M + 1 - N_{n+1, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ - \left(M + 1 - N_{n, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ \\ &= \left(M - N_{n, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ - \left(M - N_{n, I_{n+1}} + 1\right)^+ \\ &= -1. \end{align*} Thus \(D\left(n + D(n) + 1\right) = -1\) which is a contradiction as \(D \geq 0\). Therefore, \[ \forall i \in [K], \quad N_{n,i} \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} +\infty. \]

nodes.statement: As \(h(n) \to +\infty\) we can select \(N\) such that \(\forall n \geq N: \, h(n) \geq M \). Now consider \( n \geq N \), we have \begin{align*} N_{n,i} \leq h(n) & \Rightarrow \ i \in U_n \\ & \Rightarrow U_n \neq \emptyset \\ & \Rightarrow I_{n+1} \in \arg\min_{j \in U_n} N_j(n) \\ & \Rightarrow N_{n, I_{n+1}} \leq N_{n,i} = M \end{align*} Since \( I_{n+1} \) has been selected at round \( n+1 \), we have \(N_{n+1, I_{n+1}} = N_{n, I_{n+1}} + 1 \leq M + 1\), and for \( j \neq I_{n+1} \) we have \(N_{n+1,j} = N_{n,j}\).

nodes.statement: Now define \(D(n) := \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_j(n)\right)^+\), then we have \begin{align*} D(n+1) - D(n) &= \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_{n+1, j}\right)^+ - \sum_{j=1}^K \left(M + 1 - N_{n,j}\right)^+ \\ &= \left(M + 1 - N_{n+1, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ - \left(M + 1 - N_{n, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ \\ &= \left(M - N_{n, I_{n+1}}\right)^+ - \left(M - N_{n, I_{n+1}} + 1\right)^+ \\ &= -1. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Contradiction with $D\ge0$
nodes.statement: Thus \(D\left(n + D(n) + 1\right) = -1\) which is a contradiction as \(D \geq 0\). Therefore, \[ \forall i \in [K], \quad N_{n,i} \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} +\infty. \]

nodes.statement: From the result above we have that \(\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k \to 0\) using the law of large numbers. Additionally, by using the Law of Iterated Logarithm for martingales we obtain that \[\hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log\log(N_{n,k})}{N_{n,k}}}\right) \quad a.s.\]
